test_title: PYST 29: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - GA (Held On: 17 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which of the following states is NOT covered by the Ganga Plain?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Punjab**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Ganga Plain, also known as the Indo-Gangetic Plain, spans across several northern and eastern states of India, including Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, and West Bengal.
 
• Punjab is geographically located in the northwestern part of India and is primarily part of the Indus Basin, not the Ganga Basin.
 
• The Ganga Plain is characterized by fertile alluvial soil deposited by the Ganga River and its tributaries, supporting dense agriculture.
 
• Haryana, despite being geographically close to Punjab, has a small portion in the Yamuna-Ganga Plain region, making it partially included in the Ganga Plain.
 
• West Bengal and Bihar are major regions in the eastern Ganga Plain, receiving significant contributions from the Ganga and its tributaries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indo-Gangetic Plain:**

 
 
• It is one of the largest and most fertile plains in the world, covering northern and eastern India, parts of Pakistan, Nepal, and Bangladesh.
 
• It is primarily drained by the Ganga, Brahmaputra, and Indus river systems.
 
• The plain plays a critical role in India's agriculture, producing major crops like wheat, rice, sugarcane, and pulses.
 
 
 
• **Punjab Geography:**
 
 
• Punjab lies in the Indus Basin and is mainly drained by the Sutlej, Beas, and Ravi rivers.
 
• The state is known for its extensive canal irrigation system and is called the "Granary of India" due to its agricultural dominance.
 
 
 
• **Ganga River System:**
 
 
• The Ganga River originates from the Gangotri Glacier in Uttarakhand and flows through several states before emptying into the Bay of Bengal.
 
• Major tributaries include Yamuna, Gandak, Kosi, and Son.
 
• The river basin supports over 500 million people, making it one of the most densely populated regions globally.
 
 
 
• **Haryana's Ganga Plain Connection:**
 
 
• Haryana is partially included in the Yamuna-Ganga Plain due to the Yamuna River flowing through the state.
 
• Its geographical connection to the Ganga Plain is limited but significant in terms of irrigation and agriculture.
